title: 2 Things You Didn't Know About the Ferrari Purosangue

scenes.text: Ferrari closed the order book on its first four-door car before it had delivered a single one. The Ferrari Purosangue has no anti-roll bars at all. And its chief executive asked the world not to call it an SUV. These are two of the things you may not know about the Ferrari Purosangue: how its suspension works, and why Ferrari stopped taking orders. Everything here is sourced.
scenes.caption: 2 THINGS YOU DIDN'T KNOW ABOUT THE FERRARI PUROSANGUE

scenes.text: We read Wikipedia, Motor1, Robb Report, Carscoops, autoevolution, Autocar, Autoblog and a Czech business site that analysed Ferrari's results. Ferrari's own performance figures are claims, and we mark them as claims. Prices conflict between sources, and we show every one. And our own arithmetic is always labelled as ours.
scenes.caption: SOURCES: WIKIPEDIA · MOTOR1 · ROBB REPORT · CARSCOOPS · AUTOEVOLUTION · AUTOCAR · AOL/AUTOBLOG · AUTOHLED · FERRARI FIGURES ARE CLAIMS · OUR ARITHMETIC IS LABELLED

scenes.text: Motor1's Brian Silvestro, reviewing the Purosangue in July twenty twenty-four, describes its suspension in detail. The dampers are Multimatic's True Active Spool Valve type, which use electric motors to control damping and ride height. The left and right sides work independently, and the review says there are no sway bars.
scenes.caption: MOTOR1 (BRIAN SILVESTRO, 2 JULY 2024): MULTIMATIC 'TRUE ACTIVE SPOOL VALVE' DAMPERS · ELECTRIC MOTORS CONTROL DAMPING AND RIDE HEIGHT · LEFT/RIGHT INDEPENDENT · NO SWAY BARS
scenes.chapter: Thing one: the suspension with no anti-roll bars

scenes.text: The review says that in soft mode the car is composed but firm, and that hard mode stiffens the dampers and greatly reduces body roll. Silvestro writes that it handles more like a sports sedan than a crossover. We cannot measure that ourselves, and the review reports no cornering numbers, so it is one reviewer's judgement.
scenes.caption: SOFT: 'COMPOSED BUT FIRM' · HARD: 'STIFFENS THE DAMPERS AND GREATLY REDUCES BODY ROLL' · 'HANDLES MORE LIKE A SPORTS SEDAN THAN A CROSSOVER' (MOTOR1) · NO CORNERING DATA GIVEN

scenes.text: The same review gives its verdict. It calls the Purosangue the best SUV-shaped vehicle he has ever driven, and says it is not even close. It names the Cadillac CT five V Blackwing and the BMW M five CS as the closest rivals, and says the Ferrari is more enjoyable on twisty roads. The review does not compare it with the Rolls-Royce Cullinan.
scenes.caption: MOTOR1: 'BEST SUV-SHAPED VEHICLE I'VE EVER DRIVEN, AND IT'S NOT EVEN CLOSE' · CLOSEST RIVALS: CADILLAC CT5-V BLACKWING, BMW M5 CS · NO CULLINAN COMPARISON

scenes.text: Wikipedia gives the base hardware. A six point five litre naturally aspirated V12, called the F one forty IA, with seven hundred fifteen horsepower, seven hundred twenty-five metric, at seventy-seven fifty rpm, and five hundred twenty-eight pound-feet at sixty-two fifty. It drives all four wheels through an eight-speed dual-clutch gearbox, with a redline of eighty-two fifty.
scenes.caption: 6.5 L (6,496 CC) F140 IA V12: 715 HP (725 PS) @ 7,750 RPM · 528 LB-FT @ 6,250 RPM · REDLINE 8,250 · 8-SPEED DCT · AWD (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, seven hundred fifteen horsepower from six point five litres is one hundred ten horsepower per litre, with no turbochargers. Ferrari's claims, per Wikipedia: zero to one hundred kilometres per hour in three point three seconds, zero to two hundred in ten point six, and a top speed of over three hundred ten kilometres per hour. By our arithmetic, the gap from one hundred to two hundred is seven point three seconds.
scenes.caption: 715 ÷ 6.5 ≈ 110 HP/LITRE, NO TURBOS · FERRARI CLAIMS: 0–100 3.3 S · 0–200 10.6 S · >310 KM/H · 10.6 − 3.3 = 7.3 S (WIKIPEDIA; OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Motor1 lists zero to sixty at three point two seconds, but labels it as estimated, not measured. Its spec sheet gives a top speed of one hundred ninety-two miles per hour, which is three hundred nine kilometres an hour by our arithmetic. Wikipedia's figure is over three hundred ten. The numbers are close but not identical, and all of them come from Ferrari's side.
scenes.caption: MOTOR1: 0–60 3.2 S 'ESTIMATED, NOT MEASURED' · TOP SPEED 192 MPH ≈ 309 KM/H (OUR ARITHMETIC) vs WIKIPEDIA >310 KM/H · ALL FROM FERRARI'S SIDE

scenes.text: The second thing. Robb Report says Ferrari temporarily closed the Purosangue's order book about two and a half months after its debut, because interest far outpaced what it could build. The waiting list was roughly two years. And Enrico Galliera, Ferrari's chief marketing officer, said: We had such an interest without delivering one single car.
scenes.caption: ROBB REPORT: ORDER BOOK CLOSED ~2.5 MONTHS AFTER DEBUT · WAITING LIST ~2 YEARS · ENRICO GALLIERA (CMO): 'WE HAD SUCH AN INTEREST WITHOUT DELIVERING ONE SINGLE CAR'
scenes.chapter: Thing two: the order book that closed

scenes.text: Carscoops adds that on the earnings call in May twenty twenty-three, chief executive Benedetto Vigna said Ferrari was preparing to reopen orders. He said the company had been caught by positive surprise by the strong interest. Anyone who ordered then would wait until at least twenty twenty-six. Motor1 later reported that order books were at their highest levels.
scenes.caption: CARSCOOPS (5 MAY 2023): VIGNA: 'CAUGHT BY POSITIVE SURPRISE' · ORDERS REOPENING · DELIVERY 2026 AT EARLIEST · MOTOR1 (Q3 2023): ORDER BOOKS 'AT HIGHEST LEVELS'

scenes.text: There was a promise attached. Robb Report, Carscoops and Motor1 all say the Purosangue will make up no more than twenty percent of Ferrari's output. Carscoops says Vigna also pledged not to extend the model's life cycle, despite the demand. That means the promise is a ceiling on volume and a limit on time, both stated by the company.
scenes.caption: PUROSANGUE ≤ 20% OF FERRARI OUTPUT (ROBB REPORT; CARSCOOPS; MOTOR1) · VIGNA: NO EXTENSION OF LIFE CYCLE DESPITE DEMAND (CARSCOOPS)

scenes.text: Put numbers on that cap. A Czech business site reports that Ferrari delivered thirteen thousand, six hundred forty cars in twenty twenty-five. By our arithmetic, twenty percent of that is two thousand, seven hundred twenty-eight. That is a ceiling, not a count, and the article does not say how many Purosangues were delivered.
scenes.caption: 13,640 DELIVERIES IN 2025 (AUTOHLED) × 20% = 2,728 MAX (OUR ARITHMETIC) · ACTUAL PUROSANGUE COUNT: NOT GIVEN

scenes.text: An analyst once guessed at the volume. In August twenty seventeen, Autocar quoted analyst Max Warburton estimating two thousand to three thousand units a year for the model he called the FUV. By our arithmetic, that is almost exactly the range implied by the twenty percent cap on twenty twenty-five deliveries. It is an estimate made five years before the car appeared.
scenes.caption: WARBURTON (AUTOCAR, 4 AUG 2017): 2,000–3,000 UNITS A YEAR · CAP ON 2025 DELIVERIES = UP TO 2,728 (OUR ARITHMETIC) · ESTIMATE MADE 5 YEARS BEFORE THE CAR

scenes.text: Early shipments give a sense of Ferrari's scale. Carscoops reports three thousand, five hundred sixty-seven units shipped in the first quarter of twenty twenty-three, up nine point seven percent. If twenty percent of a quarter like that were Purosangues, by our arithmetic it would be about seven hundred fourteen cars. That is a hypothetical ceiling, since the car was still ramping up.
scenes.caption: Q1 2023 SHIPMENTS 3,567 (+9.7%) (CARSCOOPS) × 20% ≈ 714 (OUR ARITHMETIC; HYPOTHETICAL CEILING; MODEL STILL RAMPING UP)

scenes.text: Third, the name. Wikipedia says Purosangue is Italian for the horse breed, with a link to Purosangue Orientale, the Arabian type. In twenty twenty, Ferrari tried to trademark the name, but the Purosangue Foundation blocked it. Ferrari sued, and the case went to court on the fifth of March twenty twenty-one.
scenes.caption: PUROSANGUE = HORSE BREED (PUROSANGUE ORIENTALE) · 2020: FERRARI TRADEMARK ATTEMPT BLOCKED BY THE PUROSANGUE FOUNDATION · COURT 5 MARCH 2021 (WIKIPEDIA) · OUTCOME OF THE CASE: NOT GIVEN

scenes.text: The page does not tell us how the case ended. But Ferrari kept the name for the car, which was revealed on the thirteenth of September twenty twenty-two. Wikipedia also says Ferrari does not call it an SUV, but an FUV, a Ferrari Utility Vehicle, and has denied building an SUV on multiple occasions.
scenes.caption: REVEAL 13 SEPT 2022 (WIKIPEDIA) · FERRARI: 'FUV', NOT SUV · VIGNA AT UNVEILING (BLOOMBERG, VIA AUTOEVOLUTION): 'IT'S A FERRARI ... PLEASE DON'T CALL IT AN SUV, BECAUSE IT ISN'T'

scenes.text: Wikipedia also records an award. The Purosangue won the Compasso d'Oro industrial design award in twenty twenty-four. The page gives no jury statement or reasons, so we do not know what the judges praised. The design itself came from the Ferrari Styling Centre under Flavio Manzoni, according to the infobox.
scenes.caption: COMPASSO D'ORO 2024 (WIKIPEDIA) · JURY REASONS: NOT GIVEN · DESIGN: FERRARI STYLING CENTRE, FLAVIO MANZONI (INFOBOX)

scenes.text: The rear doors are unusual. Wikipedia says they open from the front, with a fixed B-pillar, to help access to the rear seats. The infobox calls them coach doors, while the text calls them front-opening or suicide-style. Autoevolution adds that the car has two individual rear seats and two front displays instead of one central screen.
scenes.caption: REAR DOORS FRONT-HINGED, FIXED B-PILLAR (WIKIPEDIA; INFOBOX SAYS 'COACH DOORS') · TWO INDIVIDUAL REAR SEATS · TWO FRONT DISPLAYS (AUTOEVOLUTION)

scenes.text: Motor1 says the cabin has four seats, there is no rear bench option, and the cargo area is sixteen point seven cubic feet. The reviewer calls it a real trunk that handled a road trip. Cars dot com lists seventeen cubic feet to the first row of seats and nine to the second, and four seats in total.
scenes.caption: CARGO 16.7 CU FT, NO REAR BENCH OPTION (MOTOR1) · CARS.COM: 17 CU FT (TO SEAT 1) / 9 CU FT (TO SEAT 2) · 4 SEATS

scenes.text: The criticisms. Motor1 dislikes the touch-capacitive steering wheel and climate controls, and says they should have no place in cars. It also notes that with Apple CarPlay active, the gauge cluster shows only speed, gear and fuel level, and no tachometer. For a car with an eighty-two fifty rpm redline, that detail is awkward.
scenes.caption: MOTOR1: TOUCH-CAPACITIVE WHEEL/CLIMATE CONTROLS 'SHOULDN'T HAVE A PLACE IN CARS' · WITH CARPLAY THE CLUSTER SHOWS ONLY SPEED, GEAR, FUEL: NO TACHOMETER · REDLINE 8,250 RPM

scenes.text: Dimensions, from Wikipedia: length four thousand, nine hundred seventy-three millimetres, width two thousand, twenty-eight, height fifteen eighty-nine, wheelbase three thousand eighteen. Kerb weight two thousand, one hundred seventy kilograms, which is forty-seven eighty-four pounds by our arithmetic, matching Motor1's spec sheet. Weight distribution, says Motor1, is forty-nine front, fifty-one rear.
scenes.caption: L 4,973 · W 2,028 · H 1,589 · WB 3,018 MM · KERB 2,170 KG = 4,784 LB (OUR ARITHMETIC; MOTOR1 AGREES) · 49/51 DISTRIBUTION (MOTOR1)

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, seven hundred fifteen horsepower on two thousand, one hundred seventy kilograms is about three hundred thirty horsepower per tonne. Motor1 describes the car as handling more like a sports sedan, and the Ferrari's V12 is, in the reviewer's words, special. We do not have a measured power-to-weight comparison from any source.
scenes.caption: 715 HP ÷ 2.170 t ≈ 330 HP/TONNE (OUR ARITHMETIC) · MOTOR1: 'THE V-12 ENGINE IS SPECIAL'

scenes.text: Fuel economy is where the V12 shows. Wikipedia lists the EPA rating as eleven miles per gallon in the city, fifteen on the highway and twelve combined, which it converts to nineteen point six litres per hundred kilometres combined. By our arithmetic, that conversion is correct. The Cullinan's combined rating is fourteen miles per gallon, in the Cars dot com comparison.
scenes.caption: EPA 11/15/12 MPG; 12 MPG = 19.6 L/100 KM (WIKIPEDIA; 235.2 ÷ 12 = 19.6 CHECKS) · CULLINAN 12/19/14 (CARS.COM)

scenes.text: Motor1's reviewer argues Ferrari could have used its twin-turbo V8 instead and still sold as many cars. That is an opinion, and Ferrari has not said so. But it points at the heart of the car: the naturally aspirated V12 peaks late, at sixty-two fifty rpm for torque, so you must rev it to build speed, which the reviewer says makes it more engaging.
scenes.caption: MOTOR1 OPINION: COULD HAVE USED THE TWIN-TURBO V8 AND SOLD AS MANY · V12 TORQUE PEAKS LATE (6,250 RPM) · 'MORE ENGAGING' = REVIEWER'S VIEW

scenes.text: And the sound. Motor1 says the V12 has a high-pitched exhaust note from its quad tips. Ferrari's own redline is eighty-two fifty, and Wikipedia's power peak is at seventy-seven fifty. By our arithmetic, that leaves five hundred rpm between the power peak and the redline.
scenes.caption: POWER PEAK 7,750 RPM · REDLINE 8,250 RPM → 500 RPM BETWEEN (WIKIPEDIA; OUR ARITHMETIC) · MOTOR1: HIGH-PITCHED NOTE, QUAD TIPS

scenes.text: Prices conflict, so we list them. Robb Report: three hundred ninety thousand euros, about four hundred three thousand dollars. AOL: three hundred ninety-eight thousand, three hundred fifty dollars including a five thousand dollar destination charge, before any gas guzzler tax. Carscoops: four hundred thirty thousand dollars. Motor1: four hundred twenty-three thousand, six eighty-six for the twenty twenty-five model.
scenes.caption: ROBB REPORT €390,000 (~$403,000) · AOL 2024 $398,350 INCL. $5,000 DEST. · CARSCOOPS $430,000 · MOTOR1 2025 BASE $423,686 · CARS.COM 2026 $423,636

scenes.text: By our arithmetic, the gap between AOL's twenty twenty-four price and Motor1's twenty twenty-five price is twenty-five thousand, three hundred thirty-six dollars, or six point four percent. It could reflect a model-year increase, but none of the sources say so. And Motor1's as-tested price for its review car was five hundred six thousand, three hundred five.
scenes.caption: $423,686 − $398,350 = $25,336 = +6.4% (OUR ARITHMETIC; REASON NOT STATED) · MOTOR1 REVIEW CAR AS TESTED $506,305

scenes.text: Put the starting price in context with the Census Bureau's median household income for twenty twenty-four, eighty-three thousand, seven hundred thirty dollars. By our arithmetic, three hundred ninety-eight thousand, three hundred fifty is four point eight years of that income, before tax. And Kelley Blue Book's August twenty twenty-six average new vehicle price of fifty thousand, eighty-nine makes it about eight times the average.
scenes.caption: $398,350 ÷ $83,730 ≈ 4.8 YEARS OF MEDIAN HOUSEHOLD INCOME · ÷ $50,089 AVERAGE NEW VEHICLE ≈ 7.95× (CENSUS; KBB; OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The car's internal code was F one seventy-five, according to Wikipedia. Development started in twenty seventeen. The page says Ferrari officially confirmed the project in September twenty eighteen, after Sergio Marchionne, then Ferrari's chief executive, had hinted at it. A test mule based on a GTC4Lusso appeared online on the twenty-second of October twenty eighteen.
scenes.caption: CODE F175 · DEVELOPMENT START 2017 · OFFICIAL CONFIRMATION SEPT 2018 · TEST MULE (GTC4LUSSO-BASED) SPOTTED 22 OCT 2018 (WIKIPEDIA)
scenes.chapter: The long road to the reveal

scenes.text: Leaked images appeared in February twenty twenty-two, and a month later Ferrari showed a partial image. The car was revealed in Maranello on the thirteenth of September twenty twenty-two, as a twenty twenty-three model. By our arithmetic, the span from the first spy photo to the reveal is three years, ten months and twenty-two days.
scenes.caption: LEAKS FEB 2022 · PARTIAL IMAGE A MONTH LATER · REVEAL 13 SEPT 2022 (WIKIPEDIA) · 22 OCT 2018 → 13 SEPT 2022 = 3 YR 10 MO 22 D (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: From the start of development in twenty seventeen to the reveal in September twenty twenty-two is about five years. And from the interview in which Marchionne said you would have to shoot him first, in twenty sixteen, it is about six years. Marchionne died two years after that interview, autoevolution says, so he never saw the car.
scenes.caption: 2017 → SEPT 2022 ≈ 5 YEARS · 2016 'SHOOT ME FIRST' → SEPT 2022 ≈ 6 YEARS · MARCHIONNE DIED ~2 YEARS AFTER THE INTERVIEW (AUTOEVOLUTION; OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Wikipedia says the Purosangue shares a platform with the Ferrari Roma, and autoevolution says the Roma is related to the Portofino. The transmission is a Magna eight-speed dual-clutch unit. Wikipedia describes the layout as a front mid-engine, all-wheel-drive car, so the V12 sits behind the front axle, not above it.
scenes.caption: SHARES PLATFORM WITH ROMA (WIKIPEDIA); ROMA RELATED TO PORTOFINO (AUTOEVOLUTION) · MAGNA 8DCL900 8-SPEED DCT · FRONT MID-ENGINE, AWD (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: Autocar's report from August twenty seventeen shows how the story looked before the car existed. Marchionne said an SUV-like vehicle would probably happen, but Ferrari style, and that no decision had been made. A Ferrari spokesman said Ferrari would not be launching an SUV. The same company was saying both things in the same month.
scenes.caption: AUTOCAR, 4 AUG 2017: MARCHIONNE: 'WILL PROBABLY HAPPEN, BUT ... FERRARI STYLE'; 'NO DECISION HAS BEEN MADE YET' · UNNAMED SPOKESMAN: FERRARI 'WILL NOT BE LAUNCHING AN SUV'

scenes.text: Enrico Galliera, Ferrari's commercial chief, told Autocar in the same period: We are not producing an SUV, because an SUV is not a sports car. He also ruled out a four-door model. And in an Autocar India interview he said the GTC4Lusso is our idea of an SUV. The Purosangue, five years later, has four doors.
scenes.caption: GALLIERA (AUTOCAR UK, 2017): 'WE ARE NOT PRODUCING AN SUV, BECAUSE AN SUV IS NOT A SPORTS CAR' · RULED OUT A 4-DOOR · AUTOCAR INDIA: 'GTC4LUSSO IS OUR IDEA OF AN SUV' · 2022: PUROSANGUE HAS FOUR DOORS

scenes.text: The business backdrop matters. Carscoops reports Ferrari's core earnings rose twenty-seven percent in the first quarter of twenty twenty-three, with adjusted EBITDA of five hundred thirty-seven million euros and a margin of thirty-seven point six percent. By our arithmetic, that implies revenue of about one point four three billion euros for the quarter.
scenes.caption: ADJ. EBITDA €537M, MARGIN 37.6%, +27% (CARSCOOPS) · €537M ÷ 0.376 ≈ €1.43B QUARTERLY REVENUE (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: The Czech business site Autohled reports Ferrari's twenty twenty-five revenue at seven point one four six billion euros on thirteen thousand, six hundred forty cars. By our arithmetic, that is about five hundred twenty-four thousand euros per car. That figure includes Formula One, sponsorship and brand income, so it is not the average price of a car.
scenes.caption: 2025 REVENUE €7.146B ÷ 13,640 CARS ≈ €524K PER CAR, INCLUDING F1/SPONSORSHIP/BRAND (AUTOHLED; OUR CHECK) · NOT AN AVERAGE CAR PRICE

scenes.text: Vigna, quoted by Motor1 in late twenty twenty-three, said order books were at their highest levels, and that internal combustion still has a lot to do. Motor1 notes the lineup then had seven combustion models and four hybrids, a new Maranello factory was set to open in June twenty twenty-four, and the first electric Ferrari was on track for late twenty twenty-five.
scenes.caption: VIGNA (MOTOR1, Q3 2023): ORDER BOOKS 'AT HIGHEST LEVELS' · 'ICE STILL HAS A LOT TO DO' · 7 ICE + 4 HYBRID MODELS · NEW FACTORY JUNE 2024 · FIRST EV LATE 2025

scenes.text: Autohled lists the Luce as the brand's first fully electric model in twenty twenty-five, alongside the F eighty hypercar, whose deliveries began in the fourth quarter. The Purosangue is not mentioned as a share of the total. So we know the cap, twenty percent, and the lineup, but not how close the car is to that ceiling.
scenes.caption: AUTOHLED: LUCE = FIRST FULLY ELECTRIC FERRARI (2025) · F80 DELIVERIES BEGAN Q4 2025 · PUROSANGUE SHARE OF DELIVERIES: NOT GIVEN

scenes.text: The AOL article notes that Ferrari buyers often add five or six figures in options, and that the adaptive suspension comes as standard. Motor1's review car cost five hundred six thousand, three hundred five dollars as tested. By our arithmetic, against the twenty twenty-four starting price, that is one hundred seven thousand, nine hundred fifty-five dollars of options and extras.
scenes.caption: MOTOR1 REVIEW CAR $506,305 AS TESTED − $398,350 (AOL 2024 BASE) = $107,955 = 27.1% (OUR ARITHMETIC; MODEL YEARS MAY DIFFER)

scenes.text: Against Motor1's own twenty twenty-five base price of four hundred twenty-three thousand, six hundred eighty-six, the same car carries eighty-two thousand, six hundred nineteen dollars of extras, or nineteen and a half percent. The two bases differ, so the range of options spending is nineteen to twenty-seven percent, depending on which base you trust.
scenes.caption: $506,305 − $423,686 = $82,619 = 19.5% (OUR ARITHMETIC) · RANGE 19.5%–27.1% DEPENDING ON BASE PRICE USED

scenes.text: AOL also says the price excludes any gas guzzler tax, because the government had not yet classified the car. Wikipedia's page on the Rolls-Royce Cullinan says that car is not exempt from the tax, since it is classified as a station wagon. We found no source stating the final tax for the Purosangue, so the real cost may be higher.
scenes.caption: AOL: PRICE EXCLUDES GAS GUZZLER TAX (CAR NOT YET CLASSIFIED) · CULLINAN NOT EXEMPT (CLASSIFIED AS STATION WAGON) (WIKIPEDIA) · PUROSANGUE FINAL TAX: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Sources disagree on weight, too. Wikipedia and Motor1 give four thousand, seven hundred eighty-four pounds. Cars dot com lists a base curb weight of forty-eight fifty. By our arithmetic, that is sixty-six pounds, or one point four percent, more. It is small, but it is another reminder that even a Ferrari's published numbers do not always agree.
scenes.caption: WIKIPEDIA/MOTOR1 4,784 LB vs CARS.COM 4,850 LB → +66 LB = +1.4% (OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: A last comparison, to set up the rest of this series. The Rolls-Royce Cullinan is five thousand, three hundred forty-one millimetres long and weighs two thousand, six hundred sixty kilograms, according to Wikipedia. By our arithmetic, it is three hundred sixty-eight millimetres longer than the Purosangue, seven percent, and four hundred ninety kilograms heavier, twenty-three percent.
scenes.caption: CULLINAN 5,341 MM / 2,660 KG vs PUROSANGUE 4,973 MM / 2,170 KG → +368 MM (+7.4%) · +490 KG (+22.6%) (WIKIPEDIA; OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Autoevolution says the unveiling price was alleged to be almost four hundred thousand dollars, and quotes Vigna at the unveiling as saying: It's a Ferrari. Please don't call it an SUV, because it isn't. We have kept the word SUV in this video's title for clarity. Ferrari's word is FUV, and Wikipedia says the company has denied building an SUV on multiple occasions.
scenes.caption: AUTOEVOLUTION (17 SEPT 2022): ALLEGED PRICE ~ $400,000 · VIGNA: 'IT'S A FERRARI ... PLEASE DON'T CALL IT AN SUV, BECAUSE IT ISN'T' · FERRARI TERM: FUV (WIKIPEDIA)

scenes.text: Marchionne's most direct statement came at a press conference at the New York Stock Exchange. NBC reports he said: We're dead serious about this. He also said Ferrari needed to learn how to master the relationship between exclusivity and scarcity of product. Drive dot com adds that it would be the only four-door Ferrari, built in limited numbers, and that Bloomberg reported about thirty months to settle the final production details.
scenes.caption: MARCHIONNE (NYSE PRESS CONFERENCE; NBC; DRIVE.COM.AU): 'WE'RE DEAD SERIOUS ABOUT THIS' · 'MASTER ... EXCLUSIVITY AND SCARCITY OF PRODUCT' · ONLY 4-DOOR FERRARI, LIMITED NUMBERS · ~30 MONTHS TO FINALISE (BLOOMBERG) · ARTICLES GIVE NO DATE

scenes.text: NBC set the market context. Light trucks, it says, were nearly two thirds of new vehicle sales in the United States. Bentley's Bentayga was rapidly becoming its top seller. Aston Martin showed the DBX concept at Geneva in twenty fifteen, and believed it could virtually double the company's size. Lamborghini and Rolls-Royce were developing utility vehicles of their own.
scenes.caption: NBC: LIGHT TRUCKS ~2/3 OF US NEW-VEHICLE SALES · BENTAYGA RAPIDLY BECOMING BENTLEY'S TOP SELLER · ASTON MARTIN DBX CONCEPT GENEVA 2015, COULD 'VIRTUALLY DOUBLE' ASTON'S SIZE · LAMBORGHINI AND ROLLS-ROYCE DEVELOPING UTILITY VEHICLES

scenes.text: For the rest of the practical numbers, Cars dot com lists the Purosangue with a basic warranty of three years, a wheelbase of one hundred nineteen inches, and an overall length of one hundred ninety-six. The Cullinan on the same page has four years, one hundred thirty inches and two hundred ten. By our arithmetic, the Rolls is eleven inches longer in wheelbase and fourteen in length.
scenes.caption: PUROSANGUE: 3-YR WARRANTY · 119-IN WHEELBASE · 196-IN LENGTH · CULLINAN: 4-YR · 130 IN · 210 IN → +11 IN WHEELBASE, +14 IN LENGTH (CARS.COM; OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Check Wikipedia's fuel conversions. Eleven miles per gallon in the city is twenty-one point four litres per hundred kilometres, by our arithmetic, and fifteen on the highway is fifteen point seven. Both match the page. At the regular gasoline price of four dollars, twenty-eight cents a gallon from the Energy Information Administration, twelve miles per gallon costs about thirty-six cents a mile.
scenes.caption: 235.2 ÷ 11 = 21.4 · ÷ 15 = 15.7 L/100 KM ✓ (OUR CHECK OF WIKIPEDIA) · $4.284 ÷ 12 = $0.357/MILE (EIA REGULAR, 19 OCT 2026; OUR ARITHMETIC) · REQUIRED FUEL GRADE: NOT IN OUR SOURCES

scenes.text: Specific output is another way to see the engine. The Purosangue makes about one hundred ten horsepower per litre. By our arithmetic, the Cullinan's six point seven five litre twin-turbo, at five hundred sixty-three horsepower, makes about eighty-three. Ferrari gets thirty-two percent more per litre, and does it without forced induction, though it needs to spin to eighty-two fifty to do it.
scenes.caption: PUROSANGUE 715 ÷ 6.5 ≈ 110.0 HP/L · CULLINAN 563 ÷ 6.75 ≈ 83.4 HP/L → +31.9% (WIKIPEDIA; OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: Torque tells the opposite story. Five hundred twenty-eight pound-feet from the Ferrari at sixty-two fifty rpm, against six hundred twenty-seven from the Rolls-Royce at sixteen hundred. By our arithmetic, the Cullinan has nineteen percent more torque, and reaches its peak at a quarter of the engine speed. The two engines are built for different kinds of driving.
scenes.caption: FERRARI 528 LB-FT @ 6,250 RPM vs ROLLS-ROYCE 627 LB-FT @ 1,600 RPM → +18.8% TORQUE; PEAK AT 25.6% OF THE RPM (WIKIPEDIA; OUR ARITHMETIC)

scenes.text: What is missing. How the trademark case ended. How many Purosangues have been delivered. Why the price rose between sources. A measured, independent zero to sixty or lap time. Ferrari's own explanation of why the car has no anti-roll bars. And how the cap of twenty percent is audited, if at all.
scenes.caption: NOT IN OUR SOURCES: TRADEMARK OUTCOME · UNITS DELIVERED · REASON FOR PRICE DIFFERENCES · INDEPENDENT MEASURED PERFORMANCE · FERRARI'S SUSPENSION RATIONALE · HOW THE 20% CAP IS CHECKED
scenes.chapter: What our sources do not say

scenes.text: So the two things stand. The Purosangue's suspension has electric-motor-controlled dampers and, in Motor1's account, no sway bars. And Ferrari closed its order book before delivering one car, then promised that the model would never exceed one fifth of output. Both are in our sources. The reasons behind them are not.
scenes.caption: TWO THINGS: ACTIVE DAMPERS, NO SWAY BARS (MOTOR1) · ORDERS CLOSED BEFORE DELIVERIES; 20% CAP (ROBB REPORT; CARSCOOPS)

scenes.text: Would you want a Ferrari with four doors? Tell us in the comments.
